checkpoint_review: The Router's verdicts are largely accurate. The decision to mark 'Small scales' as untestable is correct given the image resolution and underwater diffusion of light. All anatomical checkpoints (fins, spines, head) are correctly identified as present. The Router was not too lenient; the features described are clearly visible and match the taxonomy.
artifact_review: The Router identified background texture anomalies and slight blurring at fin tips. The Perceptual Quality Auditor confirmed 'slight compression' artifacts. The Topology Boundary Auditor returned a high confidence score (0.9058), suggesting the pectoral fins are well-segmented and not fused with the background, contradicting any fear of severe melting. The Geometric Depth Auditor showed valid depth separation. The artifacts noted by the Router are minor aesthetic issues (severity ~1.5) rather than structural failures. I agree with the severity ratings; they do not significantly detract from the image's validity as a lionfish representation.
alignment_reasoning: The Fine-Grained Classifier strongly confirms the class 'lionfish' (Logit 5.79 vs 5.2 for sea urchin). All testable diagnostic checkpoints (head, body shape, striping, dorsal/pectoral/pelvic fins) are visually present and anatomically consistent with Pterois species. The high topology mask confidence supports the structural integrity of the complex fin rays.

Fin tips show minor generative blending/blur. No structural melting, fusion, or extra limbs found. The depth map confirms proper foreground-background separation. These are low-severity issues typical of high-quality generative models mimicking underwater photography.
